purpose: First same-machine dual-client script (docs/research/2026-09-20-dual-pico/design.md section 7): host (copy install, MetalRage2, account mrotesthost, patched IpDrv.dll MaxClientRate/MaxInternetClientRate=100000) launches and logs in; joiner (main install, MetalRage, account mrotest) launches and logs in, staying in the lobby with the room list open; focus_client(host) + create_pve_room (existing single-client action, room name is whatever the client auto-assigns -- this action has no room-naming field, so join_room's room_name param below is a traceability LABEL only, never matched on screen, see actions.py's join_room() docstring); join_room(joiner) (double-click the one visible room row, see actions.py's ROOM_LIST_FIRST_ROW_CLICK); set_ready(joiner); host_start_battle(); enter_battle(joiner) (no click -- mech-select is automatic, see actions.py's CHANGE_SLOT_CN_OPCODE comment); console_cmd_on(joiner, 'netspeed 100000'); a 5s settle; console_cmd_on(joiner, 'stat net'); leave_battle for both; close_client for both (flushes each instance's data/System/run-*.log). REVISED 2026-09-21 after -b.json's actual first run, which shares this same create->join->ready prefix and hit two failures there -- see experiments/dual-netspeed-b.json's purpose for the full incident and experiments/dual-netspeed-c.json's purpose for the identical fix applied to the split-out C段 (this file is the kept-unchanged pre-split reference per that file's own purpose, so the SAME reorder+fix goes here too, not a divergent one): ROOM_LIST_FIRST_ROW_CLICK corrected and DEFAULT_JOIN_ROOM_TIMEOUT_S lowered 45->20 in actions.py; idle_nudge(host) moved to right after create_pve_room PLUS a second one added right after join_room (was previously a single nudge AFTER join_room, too late -- the room's own AFK self-kick was measured firing at 60,022ms, not design.md L5's ~80s estimate). This splits the host's no-input span into three windows each kept under that measured 60s ceiling by summing actions.py's own timeout constants (focus_client switches assumed ~5s, the one non-constant in this budget, flagged as residual risk): window A (Create_CQ -> idle_nudge#1) ~16s; window B (idle_nudge#1 -> idle_nudge#2, spans join_room) ~43s (includes the now-20s Enter_SA wait + 10s join_room-room wait); window C (idle_nudge#2 -> host_start_battle's own F5 send) ~35s (includes the 20s User_State_SN wait) -- see dual-netspeed-c.json's purpose for the full per-step addition. All three comfortably under 60s (margins 44s/17s/25s). Reading the host's run-*.log for 'Client netspeed is N' afterward (design.md section 7 step 10) is a manual/analysis step done AFTER this script exits, not a runner action -- it needs no Pico/client/server interaction.
